support.title: Local treatment and endocrine therapy
support.text: Surgery and radiotherapy are coordinated by the MDT. When endocrine therapy is indicated, it has its own schedule and bone-health plan.

support.title: Pregnancy / contraception
support.text: Discuss pregnancy, fertility and contraception before treatment. Report pregnancy promptly; do not breastfeed during treatment or for 7 months afterwards. The team confirms the medicine-specific contraception duration.

questions.q: How long will I receive treatment?
questions.a: Trastuzumab 600 mg under the skin every 21 days, without a loading dose, while beneficial and tolerated. Any taxane or endocrine partner follows a separate prescription and monitoring plan.

questions.q: When is my next echo?
questions.a: Echo / MUGA every 12 weeks; around C5 for uninterrupted 21-day cycles. Existing HER2 exposure and delays affect cycle numbering; the team should give the actual due window.

questions.q: How does radiotherapy fit?
questions.a: Radiotherapy is used for a defined site or symptom when indicated. The oncology and radiation teams agree whether this medicine continues or pauses; do not infer a concurrent schedule from this card.

questions.q: Does a tumour marker replace a scan?
questions.a: No. In metastatic disease it may add information to symptoms and imaging. It should not alone determine treatment changes. In symptom-free early disease it is not routine recurrence screening.

drug_mechanisms.trastuzumab: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.

evidence.population: 596 randomised patients with HER2-positive early, locally advanced or inflammatory breast cancer; neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus SC or IV trastuzumab followed by postoperative trastuzumab to complete one year.
evidence.comparison: SC trastuzumab 600 mg versus weight-based IV trastuzumab; both groups received chemotherapy.
evidence.applicability: Indirect formulation evidence only. HannaH is not a metastatic trial and supplies no metastatic survival estimate.
evidence.qualitative_result: Long-term event-free and overall survival were similar between formulations; these results do not quantify benefit over omitting trastuzumab.

endpoints.interpretation: Early-disease formulation comparison; no metastatic efficacy attribution.
endpoints.analysis_status: Final six-year analysis, secondary endpoint; initial coprimary endpoints were drug exposure and pathological complete response.

endpoints.interpretation: No demonstrated survival difference between SC and IV; this does not compare anti-HER2 treatment with no treatment.

limitations: Early-disease population; no independent metastatic estimate.
Formulation noninferiority was evaluated using the prespecified original coprimary endpoints, not a superiority survival comparison.
evidence.harms: Cardiac dysfunction, serious hypersensitivity and injection reactions remain relevant; choose route using product-specific administration and monitoring.

sections.title: Before each visit
sections.text: Have the requested blood tests and report any new breathing symptoms before attending for treatment. Bring your medication list and the Enhertu alert card. Ask when your next heart scan is due.

sections.title: On infusion day
sections.text: Take the prescribed anti-sickness medicines as instructed. The infusion is longer the first time. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, chills, rash, dizziness, wheeze or breathing difficulty during treatment.

sections.title: Between infusions
sections.text: Nausea can continue after treatment day. Follow the scheduled and rescue anti-sickness plan, drink regularly and contact the team early if vomiting prevents fluid intake. Keep activity manageable and ask for help with fatigue.

sections.title: Scans answer different questions
sections.text: Echo/MUGA monitors heart pumping function. Cancer-response scans follow the oncology plan. A CT requested urgently for new cough or breathlessness investigates a possible treatment complication; it must not wait for a routine response scan.

sections.title: If you already have a port
sections.text: A trained nurse accesses and removes the port needle for the infusion visit, then flushes the line according to local policy. Report redness, pain, swelling or fever. A new port is an individual decision, not compulsory for everyone receiving Enhertu.

evidence.primary_endpoint: Primary endpoint: blinded-central-review PFS, previously reported. This update reports investigator-assessed PFS and overall survival.
evidence.interpretation: Trastuzumab deruxtecan delayed cancer growth and improved survival compared with the treatments studied. The two studies involved different cancer groups and should not be combined into a personal prediction. Benefits must be considered alongside lung inflammation and other side effects.
evidence.limitations: Randomised open-label trial in a selected prior-treatment population. This PFS estimate is investigator assessed and must not be mislabeled as the original primary-endpoint analysis. Population medians are not individual forecasts. All-grade ILD/pneumonitis was 16.7% with T-DXd in this longer follow-up.

items.text: NCCP specifies echo/MUGA before treatment and every 12 weeks. With uninterrupted three-week cycles, week 12 is approximately before cycle 5 and week 24 before cycle 9. items.title: Advanced-disease scans
items.text: Response assessment in advanced breast cancer is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease dynamics, sites, symptoms and treatment. Less frequent monitoring may suit indolent disease. New symptoms or suspected progression need earlier assessment. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not an automatic three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: If informative, particularly when elevated at baseline or disease is not readily measurable, tumour markers may supplement clinical assessment and imaging. A marker rise alone should not trigger a treatment change. There is no universal fixed marker timetable.

items.title: DESTINY-Breast04: previously treated HER2-low advanced breast cancer
items.text: 557 patients with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer after one or two previous chemotherapy lines; 494 had hormone-receptor-positive disease. T-DXd versus physician's-choice chemotherapy. Blinded-central-review PFS in the hormone-receptor-positive cohort; PFS and OS in all patients were key secondary endpoints. In the HR-positive cohort, median PFS was 10.1 versus 5.4 months (HR 0.51). In all patients, median PFS was 9.9 versus 5.1 months (HR 0.50) and median OS 23.4 versus 16.8 months (HR 0.64). These are the original 2022 analysis, also reproduced in EMA SmPC §5.1. The HR-negative subgroup was much smaller. The trial does not establish benefit for HER2 IHC0 tumours or every earlier treatment setting. questions.q: When do I take or receive treatment?
questions.a: One infusion on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle. The next infusion is normally three weeks later. A delayed appointment is rescheduled by the team; patients do not calculate catch-up doses. The first infusion takes 90 minutes. Later infusions may take 30 minutes if the previous infusion was tolerated. Allow extra time for assessment, anti-sickness medicines and any observation. A cannula or an existing central line can be used according to the clinical plan; there is no home pump.

questions.q: When are bloods, ECGs or echoes needed?
questions.a: Before the first dose: full blood count, kidney and liver tests, an echocardiogram or MUGA scan to measure heart pumping function, and a pregnancy test where relevant. The team checks the HER2 result, previous treatment, lung history and current breathing symptoms, and agrees how disease response will be assessed. Repeat cardiac imaging every 12 weeks; assess new breathing symptoms immediately rather than waiting for the next planned scan. NCCP specifies echo/MUGA before treatment and every 12 weeks. questions.q: Which scans apply to me?
questions.a: Response assessment in advanced breast cancer is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease dynamics, sites, symptoms and treatment. Less frequent monitoring may suit indolent disease. New symptoms or suspected progression need earlier assessment. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not an automatic three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

questions.q: How long will treatment continue?
questions.a: Treatment continues while it controls the cancer and side effects remain acceptable. This advanced-disease regimen has no automatic one-year completion date. A good scan does not by itself instruct a treatment break.

questions.q: What should make me call today?
questions.a: Contact the oncology team urgently for any new or worsening cough, breathlessness or fever: lung inflammation can start at any point and can become serious. Do not wait until the next infusion or scan. Also report fever or feeling acutely unwell, unusual bleeding, inability to keep fluids down, chest pain or new ankle swelling. Severe breathing difficulty or collapse needs emergency care.

questions.q: What is my bone-health plan?
questions.a: Enhertu alone does not require a routine bone-density scan schedule. DEXA, bone medicines or bone scans are added for another treatment, fracture risk, symptoms or disease assessment when indicated.

agents.explanation: The antibody component recognises Trop-2 on cancer cells. evidence.title: ASCENT evidence in previously treated triple-negative breast cancer
evidence.population: ASCENT studied people with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after previous treatment.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review in the population without baseline brain metastases.
evidence.interpretation: Sacituzumab delayed cancer growth and improved survival in the trial. The main early analysis and the later full-study analysis used different patient groups, so their results are described separately in the clinical evidence. Your benefit and side effects may differ from the study averages.
evidence.limitations: The primary analysis excluded baseline brain metastases; the overall-population estimates differ. Open-label design, selected trial fitness and previous-treatment requirements limit extrapolation. Group medians do not predict an individual patient's benefit. This trial does not establish eligibility for every broader current EU indication.

chapters.title: The exact treatment being discussed

items.title: Who this covers
items.text: NCCP00794a covers adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior systemic therapies, including at least one for advanced disease. items.title: Dose and administration
items.text: 10 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle; prescribed reductions may apply. Premedicines, checks and at least 30 minutes of observation after every infusion add to the visit. No take-home infusion pump is part of this regimen.

items.title: Before treatment
items.text: Before the first treatment: full blood count, kidney and liver blood tests, glucose and electrolytes including magnesium, calcium and phosphate. items.title: During treatment
items.text: Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before each cycle; the neutrophil count must also meet the separate Day 8 threshold before that infusion. Glucose and the listed electrolytes are checked every second cycle. Pregnancy testing is repeated before each cycle where relevant. Review diarrhoea, hydration, nausea, oral intake, fever and infection before each infusion. Scans follow the individual response-assessment plan.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: An ECG is used when clinically indicated. Sacituzumab alone does not require a routine echocardiogram schedule. Cardiac symptoms or other medicines may change the plan.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: A routine DXA scan is not a sacituzumab-specific requirement. Bone health, bone metastases and any bone-strengthening treatment need their own individual plan.

items.title: Advanced-disease scans
items.text: Response assessment in advanced breast cancer is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease dynamics, sites, symptoms and treatment. clinical.component_rationale: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy): The antibody component recognises Trop-2 on cancer cells. Its linked SN-38 payload interferes with topoisomerase I, an enzyme involved in managing DNA during copying, which can damage dividing cells. Healthy tissues can also be affected, particularly blood-forming cells and the gut; being antibody-directed does not mean it is free of chemotherapy-type effects.

rationale.summary: Sacituzumab govitecan targets Trop-2 to deliver the topoisomerase-I inhibitor SN-38, aiming to control previously treated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.
rationale.setting: Unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two systemic therapies, including at least one for advanced disease, under NCCP00794v3.
rationale.line: Later-line TNBC within the NCCP prior-treatment criteria.
factors: Confirm triple-negative status and prior lines, including advanced-disease exposure.
Review Day 1 and Day 8 neutrophil thresholds separately.
Plan antiemetics, infusion premedication and a rapid diarrhoea/dehydration response.
Review UGT1A1-related risk, prior severe neutropenia and individual G-CSF prophylaxis.
alternatives: Other single-agent chemotherapy, biomarker-directed approaches or symptom-directed care depend on prior exposure and clinical context; ASCENT does not compare all current options.
limitations: The original ASCENT primary analysis excluded brain metastases; final overall-population results include the full randomised population. Do not mix their endpoint numbers.

evidence.population: 529 patients with relapsed/refractory metastatic TNBC, 267 assigned sacituzumab and 262 physician-choice chemotherapy; prior chemotherapy including a taxane.
evidence.comparison: Sacituzumab govitecan versus eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine or gemcitabine.
evidence.applicability: Final full randomised population, distinct from the original 468-patient primary population without brain metastases.
evidence.qualitative_result: Sacituzumab improved disease control and survival compared with the trial chemotherapy options.

endpoints.metric: Final median PFS, all randomised patients
endpoints.interpretation: Full-population estimate; not the original no-brain-metastases primary value of 5.6 months.
endpoints.analysis_status: Final secondary efficacy analysis reported in 2024.

endpoints.metric: Final median OS, all randomised patients
endpoints.interpretation: Full-population estimate; group medians do not predict individual survival.

limitations: Original primary and final overall analyses have different populations and numbers.

clinical.component_rationale: Tucatinib reduces signalling from the internal part of HER2. It works alongside trastuzumab and capecitabine, which act in different ways. Its tablet schedule continues through the capecitabine break. The body converts capecitabine into fluorouracil, which disrupts DNA and RNA processes needed for cell growth. Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.

Tucatinib can raise creatinine through transporter effects. Assess true renal function and dehydration before adjusting capecitabine; do not dismiss a rise automatically.
The current NCCP regimen includes an alternative locally approved SC trastuzumab schedule. Record route before applying dose or missed-dose advice.
Capecitabine DPD, renal and diarrhoea rules are not tucatinib rules; do not apply a single blanket percentage reduction to all components.

rationale.summary: Tucatinib inhibits intracellular HER2 signalling, trastuzumab binds extracellular HER2, and capecitabine supplies fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy. The combination aims to control previously treated HER2-positive advanced disease.

evidence.population: 612 patients with previously treated HER2-positive locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer, including stable or active brain metastases; previously treated with trastuzumab, pertuzumab and T-DM1.

evidence.qualitative_result: Adding tucatinib improved survival and disease control in the studied population.
